obligations.title: Directory < Files < Location < Condition
obligations.evidence: RequestPolicyPhase, RequestPolicyEvent and RequestPolicyGuard now form one executable finite state machine for canonicalization, URL policy/rewrite, filesystem planning, the Directory/Files/Location/Condition evaluator, filesystem rewrite, authorization, cache classification and terminal sink admission. The guard alphabet separates transition shape from admission facts; each executable guard and transition is refined to its Verus specification. request_policy_step_preserves_invariant proves the invariant is inductive, request_policy_complete_implies_all_gates proves every completed path retained canonical/original/target policy, target authorization, original authorization after retargeting, a cache classification, a selected route and sink admission, and the retarget/cache/rejection lemmas prove stale grants are cleared, cache classification precedes the sink and rejection is absorbing. policy_ref::RequestPolicyMachine consumes the verified transition function; exhaustive reachable-state enumeration plus the policy_path fuzzer exercise arbitrary valid and invalid event sequences. Inside FilesystemPolicy, access_plan_interleaves proves the exact production source/depth order: DirectoryConfig then optional DirectoryAccess at each root-to-leaf depth, Directory own-path and DirectoryMatch, BaseFiles, FilesConfig then optional FilesAccess at each depth, DirectoryMatch Files, Location, config conditions and access conditions. condition_source_plan_exec ties the deferred Config-before-Access condition order to that tail. Configuration semantic construction and Apache compatibility are tracked by their separate obligations; this obligation covers the request phase order itself.

obligations.title: Configuration schema to sealed IR to compiler refinement
obligations.evidence: ConfigSemanticKind closes all 46 payload domains. config_semantic_kind_code_is_injective proves its executable encoding is lossless; config_semantic_seal_admit requires schema/IR kind identity and complete argument-count preservation; config_semantic_projection_admit gates every main/access compiler entry and typed getter; config_semantic_refinement_is_transitive proves actual schema, sealed-value and consumer kind equality, while substitution is rejected. Production sealing consumes exact verified On/Off, decimal/range and first-keyword constructors. Capability, stable FastCGI identity, AllowOverride, proxy/balancer health, ServerAlias, LogLevel, SSLSessionCache and RewriteMap effect payloads compile once before mutation; an exhaustive access/main table test rejects effectful schema drift. P38 pins Apache's exact physical continuation in the shared main/access logical-line assembler: only one final backslash followed by LF/CRLF is removed, no separator is inserted, indentation is preserved, and trailing whitespace/backslash runs/EOF remain literal. config_physical_lines continuously compares production with an independent byte-oriented oracle and requires equivalent physical encodings to preserve the parsed ConfigLine IR. A deterministic matrix exhausts every insertion boundary, LF/CRLF, ordered split pair, continuation chain, one-to-three-backslash run, whitespace near miss and EOF form before the long-running mutation campaign begins. Apache compatibility of complex constructors remains a differential oracle rather than an internal refinement assumption.

obligations.title: per-directory Directory; access-file interleaving
obligations.evidence: AccessStep names config versus access-file provenance and exact depth for both Directory and Files phases; access_plan_exec is the only production iteration plan, and access_plan_interleaves proves its structural equality and suffix. The access walk covers every ancestor whose effective AllowOverride permits a layer and is not bounded by DocumentRoot or an alias target (access_walk_dir_admit, I47), while policy_path_work_admit bounds every request-time ancestor vector independently of whether AllowOverride applies. Every stable descriptor snapshot is lexed through the verified transition kernel and sealed into an AccessProgram with exact section mates and semantic payloads before Scope mutation; the resulting layer is cached by file version. Access/main effectful schemas must select the same verified semantic kind. Apache-equivalence of complex constructors and filesystem discovery remain refinement assumptions.

obligations.title: Require/PolicyResult semantics
obligations.evidence: PolicyResult combinators and require_none are verified; expression integer/string comparisons run through expr_compare_ints/expr_compare_strs. P27 replaces recursive runtime glob execution with stack-safe iterative DP and consumes glob_match_resource_admit before request-controlled expression matching; exhaustive small-input tests refine both iterative dialects against the Verus fnmatch_spec/expr_glob_spec semantic oracles. A full proof that the DP implementation refines those recursive specifications remains outside Verus. P28 caps each expression value/concatenation at 1 MiB and one recursive evaluation at 4 MiB, with bounded_expansion_append_admit consumed before allocation and errors propagated fail-closed. P15 expression regexes compile through the safe-Rust non-backtracking PCRE2 compatibility frontend at configuration load; expr_regex_result proves an evaluation error cannot grant through negation, regex_engine_mode_admit excludes recursive backtracking/JIT, and the compile/capture/match resource predicates bound allocation and pattern-times-subject work. The admitted regex dialect is differentially checked against the test-only PCRE2 10.46 oracle. auth_file_immutable_admit is consumed by the no-symlink authentication-file opener; its proofs reject service ownership and group/other write authority. The authentication campaign adds byte-oriented Basic scheme admission, exact credential-cache snapshot reuse and group_provider_result, whose proof makes unavailable group data Denied even under negation. Strict UTF-8 decoding, cryptographic hash implementations, parent-chain kernel enforcement and the Rust automata backend's internal matching semantics remain outside the model.

obligations.title: PCRE2 positive grammar carries a verified admission certificate into translation
obligations.evidence: PcreGrammarState is the executable option-scope machine consumed directly by the positive parser. pcre_grammar_step_refines is the independent sequence-based transition relation: Open records the exact parent x/m option state, Close restores it, empty Close and excessive nesting reject, AtomicLineEscape has no admitted transition, and StartAnchor has no admitted transition while multiline is effective. The executable step is proved to refine that relation and preserve the stack invariant. A complete parse can call pcre_grammar_finish only with an empty scope stack; the resulting PcreGrammarCertificate binds the exact source length and the balanced/atomic-line-free/multiline-start-free facts, and translation rechecks that certificate before lowering. Regression tests cover scope restoration, unbalanced input, forbidden events and source substitution. Byte-to-event parser completeness and matching equivalence remain continuously checked against the test-only PCRE2 10.46 differential oracle; the safe-Rust automata backend remains an explicit ledger assumption.

obligations.evidence: require_none_result proved and consumed by access.rs

obligations.title: AllowOverride/AllowOverrideList/Nonfatal gate
obligations.evidence: override_mode_allows is the executable category-bit admission kernel used by OverrideMode::allows/allows_flag; htaccess_section_category_admit and htaccess_section_admit totalize every supported section command and independently gate it by its Apache category mask or exact AllowOverrideList '<Section' entry, so a listed child cannot admit an unlisted top-level wrapper. htaccess_section_nonfatal_override_admit pins Apache's fail-closed execute-on-read section subset; nested authz containers are admitted only after their outer authz command has passed while child directives remain gated. htaccess_gate_admit is the single final apply/skip/reject disposition before the effectful parser. The exhaustive parser matrix and 96 paired Apache wrapper cases cover child-only/exact lists, category masks and Nonfatal behavior.

obligations.title: htaccess/cache fast-path over-approximation
obligations.evidence: prefilter_sound proves both boolean implications in Verus: htaccess_may_apply false admits no access-file layer, while cache_base_scope_only_sound proves a path outside the inherited base enable list remains disabled when the compiler has excluded CacheEnable from every rule delta. cache_base_scope_admit is consumed at that compiler boundary. The path-pattern matcher and parser-to-ActiveLayer/rule-tree refinement remain explicit assumptions

obligations.title: ACL reachability and resource binding
obligations.evidence: I1a exact ResourceKey grants and I1b inode/backend/policy binding feed the executable TransformCapability state. ResourceKey and OutcomeIdentity carry the private-inner DecodedUrlPath rather than an interchangeable string, and every AccessGrant carries an opaque immutable configuration-generation token checked by AuthorizedPlan construction and every terminal sink. authorized_plan_identity_admit gates construction of the move-only AuthorizedPlan over one public URL, selected URL, lexical/resolved filesystem pair, scope, exact grant and resource; AuthorizedOutcome adds the admitted sink. Production file, directory, CGI, FastCGI, proxy, WebSocket and cache entry points consume this artifact rather than independently supplied fields, and local-file boundaries compare the descriptor device/inode with it. Every protected sink calls AccessGrant::require_sink, which combines generation equality, exact resource equality and the verified sink-specific admission predicate. I31 opens and reauthorizes CGI and FastCGI scripts before binding the selected inode; P15 FastCGI binds transport, lexical SCRIPT_FILENAME, authorized canonical path and PATH_INFO, with fastcgi_script_identity_admit proving that neither script identity can be omitted. P17 adds fastcgi_resolved_target_admit at the SetHandler constructor so its lexical classification/wire path cannot be replaced by the canonical authorization path. P18-B2 rebuilds a configuration-only scope for every selected ProxyPass/ProxyPassMatch or FastCGI route and consumes proxy_operator_acl_admit before the access-file-restricted scope, so access files may narrow but never supply the operator grant. Authorization providers and request-plan refinement remain outside this obligation.

obligations.title: Ordered competing request-to-resource mappings
obligations.evidence: first_match_is_first and first_match_none_means_no_match prove that the selected match bit is the first true one and that no bit means no match, so a later overlapping route cannot win; Alias/AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch and Redirect/RedirectMatch use vhost-before-main first-match tables, ProxyPass/ProxyPassMatch share one main-before-vhost route_order space, and handler operations use last-match wins. configuration_child_merge_order gives proxy routes a checked generation boundary. The multi-vhost Apache differential matrix covers both lexical placements, prefix/regex routes, two tenants and reload; flattening the runtime tables to the match-bit vector remains outside Verus

obligations.title: Every target-changing transform reauthorizes the sink
obligations.evidence: TransformCapability is an executable Verus state machine: retarget clears authorization and every binding, authorize binds the current target, and inode/backend/representation transitions add only their exact capability. transform_retarget_requires_reauthorization proves a retargeted state cannot reach any sink; transform_sink_implies_reauthorized plus the file/backend/cache lemmas prove every admitted sink has the required bindings, while transform_proxy_sink_implies_representation_bound proves endpoint binding alone cannot reach a proxy sink. AccessGrant::require_sink is the runtime projection at every protected sink, and exact ResourceKey equality makes a pre-transform grant unusable after a target change. ProxyRepresentationWitness retains the byte-exact authorized front path and upstream path; bind_proxy binds that witness and endpoint atomically, and require_proxy_sink compares it with the concrete endpoint/path immediately before WebSocket or HTTP proxy I/O, including balancer failover. The I30 inventory covers alias, CGI/FastCGI PATH_INFO and handlers, symlinks, rewrites, DirectoryIndex, ErrorDocument, DirectorySlash, proxy/balancer failover, cache targets and WebSocket.

obligations.title: Scheme, peer, canonical name and identity have trusted sources
obligations.evidence: HTTPS/REQUEST_SCHEME come from listener TLS state, UseCanonicalName uses ServerName, and identity comes from verified authenticators. HTTP authentication identity is owned by the logical Request and shared only by its internal clones; request_identity_record_admit permits the first binding and same-user confirmation while proving a conflicting overwrite impossible. Canonical-target checks and proxy failover independently authorize their targets without erasing the established identity. HTTP Host, absolute-form and HTTP/2 authorities consume parse_http_authority_endpoint, which owns complete bracket/colon splitting, registered-name validation and normalization, checked ports, and compressed or embedded-IPv4 IPv6 parsing; the runtime only renders the typed host result. Controls/whitespace, malformed percent escapes, ambiguous unbracketed literals and numeric overflow cannot enter the canonical authority identity. RemoteIP retains Apache's internal/trusted proxy classes; remoteip_next_internal and remoteip_candidate_admit mechanize the one-way class transition and rejection of private values presented by an external chain. The whole_request_differential campaign encodes each generated logical request through the production HTTP/1 parser and vendored HTTP/2 client/server codec, then requires equal canonical request bytes, request plan, authorization result, backend identity, cache classification and response semantics. The parser/walk projection and broader context-construction refinement remain partial.

obligations.title: Untrusted streams have bounded size and deadlines
obligations.evidence: I33 covers request/proxy trailer count and byte budgets, proxy chunk checked_add before resize, CGI worker path/env/body/output caps, FastCGI record/header/stdout/stderr caps, HTTP/2 budgets and compression. parse_chunk_size_hex proves the accepted digits' exact mathematical value, chunk_extension_admit and http_trailer_field_admit prove the executable grammar and exclusion of framing/routing trailer names, and chunk_framing_budget_step proves each checked transition remains within the chunk-count/framing-byte ceilings. The vendored h2 control-frame limiter charges every concrete SETTINGS, PING, PRIORITY and WINDOW_UPDATE event through h2_control_event_step, which proves exact event cost, one elapsed-time refill/epoch advance and arithmetic below the fixed burst even across multiplication overflow. resource_budget_admit and connection_admit mechanize overflow-free global/per-client admission; client_quota_ipv6_key is the executable IPv6 /64 fairness key, with proofs that the host half is zeroed and the allocation prefix is preserved. h2_process_slot_admit requires source admission before process admission, while minimum_progress_rate_admit proves the complete-second byte-rate comparison and safely rejects arithmetic overflow without extending an absolute deadline. RAII runtime leases enforce shared spool-byte/file, request/response resident-byte, response-body descriptor-read, HTTP/2-stream, asynchronous pending-connection, effective-client HTTP/1-worker, established-H2-connection and CGI/FastCGI concurrency ceilings across reloads. Spool bytes/files, retained/transient response bytes, response reads, slow-body workers and RewriteMap helpers now have source-keyed fair shares; dynamic allocation inherits effective-client identity before consuming the global pool. response_body_read_lease_admit permits only DescriptorRead and proves RequestDispatch/ClientWriteWait cannot retain that counter. OutputOwnershipPhase additionally proves outer cancellation cannot release descriptor/backend ownership while a blocking read task still owns it. PreparedHandlerKind covers every typed Proxy/FastCGI/CGI IR variant, and the runtime projects that type before leaving request-worker admission; slow backend and WebSocket regressions prove neither retains a request worker. IPv4 quotas remain exact; HTTP/1-worker, HTTP/2-stream and WebSocket admission use the validated RemoteIP effective identity; a trusted transport proxy receives only a bounded pre-header allowance and does not bypass downstream worker accounting. P20 makes both HTTP adapters consume one incremental BodyAccumulator and request_body_memory_admit proves each resident-prefix extension is bounded. Known-length dynamic uploads above 1 MiB instead use a four-chunk, resource-accounted channel in both adapters, propagating backend backpressure without full-body spooling; unknown-length/chunked uploads retain the bounded spool path required to determine CGI/FastCGI CONTENT_LENGTH. The fixed HTTP/1 identity reader charges only body chunks actually received; HTTP/2 file/stream responses wait for flow-control capacity, retain response-byte leases on 64 KiB chunks and scope response-body read leases to the read itself. Queued HTTP/2 retained and transient byte slices remain reclassifiable and own their leases until the final transport slice is released; bodyless responses likewise keep their resident-byte and general-stream leases in a queued header value until h2 encodes or discards the complete head. Compression, CGI and autoindex shrink peak-work reservations to the retained representation. Post-P31 generalization gives HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 one anchored slow-output deadline: plain asynchronous file output uses non-blocking sendfile in 256 KiB quanta, unsupported sources and TLS fall back to accounted 64 KiB reads, and a slow progressing writer completes beyond one Timeout interval. P31 and its protocol-neutral follow-up move cumulatively blocked HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 outputs exactly once from general capacity into a shared 128-process/32-per-source slow-output pool, preserving one complete advertised H2 connection per slow source while limiting it to one quarter of the reserve. slow_output_phase_step is the executable ownership transition; its proofs exclude Slow-to-General reopening and make Closed absorbing. Minimum-rate checkpoints and the absolute 16-send-interval response ceiling are anchored at response start, so a partial capacity grant cannot renew either boundary; each interval is max(Timeout, 5s), and the connection idle deadline runs only with no active stream. P27 removes recursive/backtracking runtime glob evaluation; iterative DP uses O(subject) memory, access-file lines and configuration patterns are capped at 8190 bytes, and request-controlled expression globs consume glob_match_resource_admit before allocation under a four-million-cell ceiling. P28 consumes bounded_expansion_append_admit before rewrite/expression vector growth, caps rewrite path/query output at 64 KiB, expression values at 1 MiB with a shared 4 MiB evaluation budget, and access-file recursive compilation at 64 sections through access_section_depth_admit. P29 makes access-plan execution constant-stack, consumes policy_path_work_admit before allocating any request-time ancestor vector, and caps the cumulative copied prefixes as well as component count even when AllowOverride is disabled. Static-only configurations skip CGI PATH_INFO discovery; CGI-enabled prefix probes mutate one buffer and charge each candidate's byte length to the shared request budget. Follow-up gates prove successful-only cache invalidation, autoindex scan/render arithmetic, bcrypt cost and regex compile/capture/pattern-times-subject work bounds; P24 variable repetitions include the optional terminal path and a conservative PikeVM active-set factor, with regex_optional_repeat_charge_bounds_pike_work proving dominance under the ordinary work ceiling. Runtime limits proxy and CGI responses, DNS workers, expensive CPU work and byte-counted policy/auth/access caches. Body/header parsing uses hard deadlines plus configured minimum rates; TLS and first HTTP/1 heads run in a bounded asynchronous admission pool; every keep-alive body reacquires the source-fair slow-body reserve; TLS handshake state and rate, reusable HTTP/1 workers, RewriteMap program helpers, log-line expansion/writers, useful WINDOW_UPDATE events and disk-cache administrative walks now have independent process ceilings. escape_log_bytes_bounded proves the request-derived log projection stays within the caller's complete-line limit while excluding CR, LF and NUL. The HTTP/2 preface, initial SETTINGS and first request head share the header deadline; HTTP/2 is capped at 32 streams per connection, 64 per client and 256 process-wide with client-first acquisition; ready listeners rotate through bounded accept batches; and connection spawn/descriptor exhaustion paths are regression-tested. Request-time expression and authentication-file reads reject non-regular descriptors, use O_NONBLOCK/O_NOFOLLOW and bounded reads; authentication cache hits re-open the path and require the same inode. One adapter lifecycle ledger now moves stream identity, phase, active capacity and delayed-reset capacity atomically; its verified connection-close transition zeroes both counters. Vendored SETTINGS synchronization and peer HEADERS/DATA admission consume explicit verified state machines, while a bounded terminal-cause FIFO distinguishes a genuinely closed stream from a skipped lower ID. The whole-request HTTP/1/HTTP/2 differential additionally asserts that every process, per-client, filesystem, transport and queued-output resource ledger returns to zero after each composed evaluation. Kernel/socket scheduling and remaining HPACK/codec internals are outside the model.

obligations.title: Header set/add/unset/always semantics across all response paths
obligations.evidence: Static, directory, redirect, CGI/FastCGI, proxy and error responses apply the ordered header policy; child set replaces, unset runs last, always applies to errors; merge/application proofs are unit-tested but not mechanized. Security-relevant field consumers now share complete byte-level grammars for exact fixed-point qvalues, entity-tag lists, strict Cookie pairs, all three HTTP-date forms and proxy response status lines; malformed input fails closed rather than yielding a useful prefix, and the shared entry points have a dedicated fuzz target.

obligations.title: Every positive terminal outcome enforces original-URL and current-target grants
obligations.evidence: TransformCapability plus AccessGrant::require_sink mechanize the final exact-resource and sink-binding gate for static/directory, CGI/FastCGI, proxy, WebSocket, cache and redirect outcomes. authorized_plan_identity_spec additionally requires one coherent public URL, selected URL, lexical/resolved identity and exact grant; production sink adapters consume the resulting move-only AuthorizedPlan/AuthorizedOutcome, cache lookup/store own it through CacheContext, failover replaces it atomically, and local-file adapters reject descriptor/inode substitution. Redirect, DirectoryIndex and ErrorDocument are closed TransformSink variants: every routing redirect consumes an outcome bound to the exact normalized Location and terminal status (a Location-bearing 3xx or a Location-free 4xx/5xx), while DirectoryIndex and local ErrorDocument consume an outcome additionally bound to the exact InternalRequestKind and projected target. Configured external ErrorDocument redirects use a separate move-only recovery outcome bound to the immutable generation, original error status, response status and exact configured Location rather than fabricating a resource grant after denial. Deferred internal handlers retain their outcome across body acquisition and revalidate it immediately before dispatch. The complete RequestPolicyState reference machine makes SinkAdmission a distinct phase after authorization and cache classification; request_policy_step_to_complete_implies_all_gates and request_policy_complete_implies_all_gates prove no completed trace can omit canonical/original/target policy, target authorization, required original authorization after a rewrite, route selection, cache classification or sink admission. MultiViews candidate admission additionally requires a missing public target, same-directory basename match, regular typed representation, static handler, acceptable negotiation result and bounded scan. multiview_authorization_meet_spec requires the public URL, selected URL, resolved inode and selected-name rewrite result together; dispatch consumes that admission after exact URL/path/dev/inode binding. multiview_cache_binding_spec requires cache lookup/store to use the selected URL and resolved target, and the cache planner consumes the same selected scope/rewrite transition as dispatch. Original-URL and current-target scopes are both enforced and F23 covers rewrite-then-proxy/redirect.

obligations.title: Internal request transitions preserve only kind-authorized state
obligations.evidence: InternalRequestKind and internal_request_projection are the executable transition policy consumed by the sole internal dispatcher: DirectoryIndex preserves the selected application's method, body, query and exact header/body storage, while a local ErrorDocument becomes a bodyless GET with only its configured query and the exact expected entity, conditional-range, hop-by-hop, upgrade and Connection-nominated header set removed. Both preserve the mutable request target, version and keep-alive decision as well as clone-shared wire method/target/version, request-scope lineage, authenticated identity, public URI, proxy session and resident-byte lease. Header projection and request-context/identity preservation are computed as separate facts. The runtime computes exact equality for every projected field and consumes internal_request_runtime_refines; its Verus specification is one complete conjunction, and admitted_internal_request_refines_every_field proves admission cannot omit a field. A sealed ProjectedInternalRequest carries that complete refinement into the consuming authorization boundary, so no caller can substitute a boolean certificate. Each move-only AuthorizedOutcome also stores the exact InternalRequestKind and DecodedUrlPath; internal_request_outcome_admit plus internal_request_outcome_binds_kind_target_and_projection prove the sink class, target and full runtime projection are jointly required before dispatch. error_document_depth_step owns recursion, internal_request_target_admit rejects ambiguous local targets at compile time and dispatch, directory_index_name_admit binds the literal probe to the URL component, and deferred-handler tests prove the exact projection and token are rebuilt after lazy body acquisition.

obligations.title: Dynamic execution preserves authorization, finalization, cache and output order
obligations.evidence: DynamicOutcomeState is the executable Prepared -> Backend -> Response -> Output/Aborted machine for the facts formerly implicit in nested PreparedHandler wrappers. Its initial state records the complete handler tree's required internal projection, ErrorDocument finalizer and dispatch/cache finalizer. StartBackend requires authorization, backend binding and any internal projection; BackendComplete requires a structurally valid response; cache consideration requires an admitted response, an active dispatch finalizer and the current configuration generation; output requires every required outer finalizer; Aborted is absorbing. The executable transition and readiness predicates refine their Verus specifications, and separate lemmas prove backend, cache, output and abort consequences. The move-only runtime DynamicOutcomeToken is created once from the typed handler tree and consumed immediately around the concrete proxy, FastCGI and CGI side effects, response parser, local ErrorDocument restoration, cache lookup/store and terminal response boundary; an invalid transition fails closed. A cancelled request is moved to Aborted before StartBackend, so it cannot open a proxy/FastCGI exchange or launch CGI. The whole_request_differential campaign executes those live backends for H1 and H2, compares exact proxy/FastCGI request serialization and fully finalized response semantics across fragmented, chunked, empty and malformed replies, exercises cold/warm cache, pre-sink cancellation and local/external ErrorDocument plus CGI/FastCGI/proxy DirectoryIndex, and checks the complete resource ledger after each projection. The multi_request_state campaign additionally prepares an outcome before generation retirement, access-file replacement or balancer-health mutation and proves that execution retains that immutable outcome while fresh requests observe the new state.

obligations.title: Reload advances a cache generation and stale entries are never served
obligations.evidence: cache_lookup_admit binds key/policy/Vary/generation/freshness; cache_lookup_hit_requires_binding and cache_lookup_rejects_stale mechanize the consequences. cache_generation_admit is consumed by lookup/store and stale_cache_generation_rejects_work proves unequal epochs fail closed. Each immutable Config owns a clone-shared epoch cell: request planning captures it, unsafe-method invalidation updates that generation, and reload retires the old cell while advancing the candidate. A read/write publication barrier makes an old store either precede cleanup or fail its second epoch check, so it can neither adopt the candidate epoch nor recreate files on an abandoned CacheRoot. Conditional hits consume cache_if_none_match_matches and cache_conditional_hit_admit: the strict list scanner proves star or a validated stored tag witness, weak comparison validates both opaque tags, quoted commas remain inside a candidate, empty/trailing/malformed members fail closed, and If-None-Match has precedence even on a non-match. Disk metadata records the epoch, PATH_INFO keys resolve to the actual CGI script, and verified saturating cache_expiry prevents positive-TTL wrap. The multi_request_state H1/H2 oracle warms an old entry, commits retirement and clear_reload, then requires a candidate lookup under changed authorization to deny without a stale HIT; protocol reload orchestration remains runtime-tested rather than mechanically refined

obligations.title: map_path, access-file walk and cache consume one alias-root identity
obligations.evidence: Relative AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch roots are resolved against ServerRoot at compile time and access_root_for uses the same alias table; absolute/prefix and relative/capture-only forms are unit-tested

obligations.title: Autoindex and generated headers use sink-context encoders
obligations.evidence: safe_relative_href prefixes './' before URL encoding so hostile names cannot become javascript:/data:/scheme-relative links; header values pass the verified sanitizer that now rejects every control byte except HTAB plus DEL

obligations.title: Require providers consume exactly the post-not operand
obligations.evidence: parse_require uses rest.first() for env and rest.join(' ') for expr; the verified require_env_operand_admit rejects empty or NAME=VALUE operands, require_method_operand_admit accepts only exact supported method tokens, and expression variables are load-time validated; Require::Expr and Require::ValidUser both carry negation; unit and HTTP-level tests cover the provider and negation shapes

obligations.title: Every accepted .htaccess directive is modeled, explicitly inert, or rejected
obligations.evidence: htaccess SetEnv/SetEnvIf/UnsetEnv/PassEnv and IndexIgnore populate EnvironmentPolicy/ContentPolicy through the same parser as main config; RequestHeader and every recognized-but-unimplemented metadata/presentation directive are rejected instead of accepted as inert. One immutable DirectiveRegistry is the authoritative classifier for both compilers and seals canonical identity, ownership, security disposition, main schema and access category/disposition/schema; duplicate names fail construction, and an exhaustive test asserts every access entry is present in the main vocabulary and every effectful shared directive has the same semantic payload domain. The effect matrix still requires every entry to be effectful, explicitly equivalent, or rejected and gated by AllowOverride None; I34 makes known-but-unimplemented and unknown main-config directives fail closed in every mode.

obligations.title: Autoindex policy and /dir versus /dir/ authorization
obligations.evidence: IndexIgnore filters listing entries in main config and .htaccess; DirectorySlash Off reauthorizes a no-slash directory target as the canonical trailing-slash URL before index/listing dispatch. DirectoryIndex probes and autoindex metadata use the same descriptor-relative FollowSymLinks/SymLinksIfOwnerMatch decision as live serving, so a forbidden link cannot disclose target type/size or select an index. Cache admission reuses that resolver and refuses Forbidden targets. owner_component_reopen_admit rejects a device/inode substitution between the owner walk's no-follow probe and usable reopen; unit cases cover ordinary-component substitution, owner-mismatched index links, autoindex metadata and cache admission.

obligations.title: Regex alias targets remain inside their configured alias base
obligations.evidence: map_path returns an explicit mapping failure when a capture-only or absolute AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch expansion leaves fs_path; the parent-root fallback is removed; alias admission now consumes the verified component-aware path_under_base kernel (including the /srv/www versus /srv/www2 boundary), and unit plus end-to-end F31 cases cover the escape shape

obligations.title: Internal rewrite filesystem targets never change the authorization base
obligations.evidence: verified rewrite_filesystem_shape_admit rejects external, passthrough and relative substitutions before filesystem lookup; rewrite_filesystem_candidate_admit composes that shape gate with an opened regular-file descriptor and component-aware path_under_base check. The admitted FilesystemTarget retains the original mapping root, root-relative path and opened actual path through dispatch; rewrite_filesystem_binding_admit and rewrite_filesystem_binding_rejects_reroot exclude the former target-parent re-rooting behavior. UnsafePrefixStat cannot change the authorization base, and rewrite-condition file tests use descriptor-relative RESOLVE_BENEATH probes rather than canonicalize-then-stat. A deterministic parent-replacement regression verifies the retained root rejects an outside symlink after selection. The rewrite target scope remains conjoined with both rewritten and original URL policy.

obligations.title: FastCGI script and PATH_INFO targets are bounded by the configured base
obligations.evidence: script_from_prefix cleans the script inside the FastCGI prefix or document/alias root and consumes the verified component-aware path_under_base kernel; split_path_info binds regular-file and symlink containment to one openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH descriptor check, and execution repeats that descriptor-bound check before handoff. The ancestor walk cannot select an ancestor file such as /bin/sh or a sibling with a shared byte prefix such as www2; unit cases cover dot segments, $1 templates, sibling-prefix targets and outside targets

obligations.title: Cache keys bind request inputs that select authorization branches
obligations.evidence: cache_policy_material destructures Scope and hashes every policy slice (rewrite maps canonicalized); cache_policy_fingerprint frames each exact field with the verified injective cache_fingerprint_field and uses a 256-bit SHA-256 digest instead of the old 64-bit DefaultHasher. The digest binds all request headers, peer address, method, target and HTTP protocol; CGI/FastCGI/custom-handler entries additionally bind the peer port exported to the backend, while static entries use a canonical zero port and remain reusable across connections. V7 disk metadata stores the complete base key, lookup consumes cache_disk_key_admit for an exact metadata-key match, and V6 and older metadata are deliberately ineligible after strict complete response cache-policy admission. Cache-Control is parsed across every field line with quoted-string ownership; malformed response or request policy, qualified private/no-cache, conflicting TTLs, invalid Vary and ambiguous singleton metadata fail closed. cache_trailing_slash_target_admit rejects an unchanged regular-file representation ending in slash before lookup. Successful unsafe responses invalidate the request URI plus only canonical same-origin Location/Content-Location targets; cache_invalidation_target_admit rejects cross-origin targets and cache_invalidation_remove_admit preserves unrelated keyed entries. The unit matrix mutates every policy field plus listener/vhost/URL/query/target/header/protocol/port dimensions, and F34 replay verifies header partitioning

obligations.title: Upstream request lines and forwarded headers reject control injection
obligations.evidence: request authorities consume the complete verified authority/IP parser and backend authorities are validated at configuration parse time; RewriteRule [P] templates consume rewrite_template_static so every runtime capture/variable spelling ($N, %N, \N, ${...}, %{...}) is rejected from the backend authority; X-Forwarded-Host is checked before insertion. The verified HTTP/1 head compiler selects one framing before any body read: it rejects duplicate CL or TE even when identical, CL+TE, leading empty lines, duplicate/contradictory/malformed Connection, Proxy-Connection, every unimplemented Connection nomination, un-nominated TE, and unsupported or bodyless expectations. The HTTP/2 adapter accepts one strict decimal Content-Length, canonicalizes it before CGI/FastCGI translation and checks it against DATA length. HTTP and WebSocket request construction, final-head validation, upstream write, response-line parsing and Location rewriting operate on bytes; validate_proxy_head applies proxy_request_line_admit and proxy_header_admit immediately before every upstream write. proxy_representation_witness stores the exact authorized and upstream path bytes, while require_proxy_sink checks that witness and concrete endpoint at every HTTP/WebSocket/failover sink. proxy_response_framing consumes the complete admitted field list and atomically rejects duplicate/malformed CL or TE, CL+TE and unsupported codings before selecting no-body, length, chunked or EOF framing; 205 admits only no length or exact zero length and never selects a body. CGI and file-backed FastCGI select the earliest CRLF/LF header terminator and reject ambiguous singular metadata. Proxy/CGI ingestion consumes the verified three-way backend Connection disposition: framing nominations reject, stripped end-to-end metadata is forward-only, and only ordinary options remain cacheable. Cache storage, HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 share one response-header sanitizer and complete validity gate; malformed or duplicate Connection options fail closed, nomination work is capped at 64 options and 4 KiB, fixed and nominated hop-by-hop fields are removed, and V7 cache metadata cannot replay a representation admitted under older policy. HTTP/1 emits its sole connection decision and HTTP/2 emits none. FastCGI response records are bound to the active request ID and validate reserved bytes plus END_REQUEST shape/status. Ordinary upstream sockets are single-use and advertise Connection: close. WebSocket requires HTTP/1.1 on both hops; 101 responses use the same bounded option parser, reject framing metadata and duplicate handshake fields, are reconstructed into one canonical switching head, and preserve bytes co-read after the head. Raw-query/obs-text, malformed-response and fragmented pipelining properties prove byte preservation and fail-closed parsing

obligations.title: Authenticated identity reaches CGI and FastCGI environment
obligations.evidence: the request-owned authenticated identity is retained in every access grant across resolved-target reauthorization and proxy failover; CgiContext/build_env emit REMOTE_USER and AUTH_TYPE=Basic for local CGI and FastCGI even when the canonical target scope does not repeat the lexical AuthType. Configured environment entries remain unable to override reserved names. Unit, F38 and Apache-differential symlinked-CGI cases cover isolation and lifetime.

obligations.title: Single-file aliases map to parent plus basename
obligations.evidence: prefix Alias/ScriptAlias file targets are split into parent plus basename, the access-file walk uses the parent, and handler/MIME/FastCGI selection consumes the resolved basename; alias_file_target_split, alias_access_root_admit and handler_name_from_target are mechanized and the F39 replay covers .htaccess deny plus CGI source disclosure

obligations.title: Effectful directives inside <Limit> are applied or rejected
obligations.evidence: main-configuration Options/Header/AddHandler/SetHandler inside <Limit> are applied to the enclosing scope instead of warn-and-ignored, while auth/access directives remain method-scoped; .htaccess rejects non-auth directives; limit_directive_effect is mechanized and config/unit plus F40 replay cases cover Options -ExecCGI and -Indexes

obligations.title: CGI/FastCGI reauthorize and bind the actual target
obligations.evidence: the dispatcher binds the opened target before handler selection; PATH_INFO reauthorizes fd_path(file). FastCGI now resolves the script through an open descriptor, reauthorizes its actual fd path, binds both dev/inode and the exact backend identity, and reopens plus compares dev/inode immediately before emitting SCRIPT_FILENAME. cgi_actual_target_admit is mechanized and the F41 replay covers direct, PATH_INFO and FastCGI symlink targets. Pass-11 classification (is_cgi) is a single cgi_exec_admit kernel call with fail-closed lemmas, evaluated on the lexical basename while containment stays on the resolved target.

obligations.title: Capture-only regex aliases have no implicit ServerRoot base
obligations.evidence: Alias::regex keeps an empty base for leading-capture replacements and map_path fails closed for every empty-base mapping; capture_only_alias_admit is mechanized and the F42 replay asserts .htpasswd, rewrite secrets and the configuration are not readable

obligations.title: Spool/temp files use exclusive creation and private mode
obligations.evidence: the FastCGI spool uses create_new, mode 0600, bounded collision retries and immediate unlink; temp_file_create_admit is mechanized and unit cases plant a symlink at the predicted name and verify the target is untouched and the descriptor is private

obligations.title: Disk and resident cache tiers have independent byte quotas
obligations.evidence: cache_disk_projected and cache_disk_evict mechanize replacement projection and monotone eviction; persisted bytes are tracked per cache root, CacheMaxDiskSize and MAX_DISK_ENTRIES are enforced by evicting the oldest stems, oversized entries are refused, expired/old-generation files are deleted on load, per-key variants are capped, and CacheIgnoreQueryString bypasses dynamic CGI/FastCGI/proxy targets. Store and invalidation index discovery is iterative and stops after depth 32 or 32,768 directory records; an incomplete scan refuses new stores and invalidation advances the generation and clears memory, so unvisited persisted entries cannot become eligible. The independent CacheMaxMemorySize counter includes key, body, response headers and Vary material; cache_memory_admit bounds overflow-free insertion and replacement, oldest entries are evicted under the lock, bodies above 64 KiB remain disk-only, and lookup clones an Arc rather than copying a retained body under the process-wide mutex

obligations.title: Expression file tests use the document-root confinement
obligations.evidence: Expr::FileTest consumes confined_expr_relative for -f/-d/-e/-s/-F/-U, rejecting absolute and parent-relative arguments, then inspects only a descriptor opened beneath the retained document/alias-root with openat2 RESOLVE_BENEATH. file() uses the same root-relative walk with O_NOFOLLOW/O_NONBLOCK, a 64 KiB ceiling and a before/after descriptor version check; filesize() uses descriptor metadata. Escaping symlinks therefore cannot become metadata/read oracles through a canonicalize-to-path race. Config compilation binds the effective default or explicit DocumentRoot into every global/vhost scope, and synthetic empty-root scopes fail closed rather than falling back to '/'. Main-config <IfFile> remains a separate operator-supplied execute-on-read condition; unit and P14 regressions cover absent-DocumentRoot, absolute, parent-relative and escaping-symlink cases. Rewrite condition file tests use the same descriptor-relative probe, with final no-follow metadata for -l.

obligations.title: RequireNone fails when any child provider is satisfied
obligations.evidence: combine_or_all and require_none_multi aggregate every child as an OR of positive hits before negation, so a granted child cannot be neutralized by a denied sibling; access.rs consumes require_none_multi and require_none_multi_result is the mechanized disposition predicate; main-config, .htaccess, unit and generated Apache differential cases cover two-provider and three-provider block lists

obligations.title: Regex alias file targets use parent plus basename and the parent access root
obligations.evidence: map_path splits a regex alias target that resolves to a regular file into parent plus basename with or without a trailing slash in the replacement; the URL/base root uses the file parent via alias_access_root_admit for regex and prefix aliases alike, while ancestor authorization follows I47 independently of that root; unit plus F47 replays cover AliasMatch/ScriptAliasMatch static and CGI targets

obligations.title: Virtual-host selection is bound to destination address and port
obligations.evidence: Config::select_vhost consumes vhost_address_admit and vhost_address_precedence with the destination address; address-bound vhosts are ineligible on another address and exact-address vhosts precede wildcard vhosts; HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, WebSocket, cache and logging pass the local address, TLS filters vhosts when the listener has a concrete address, and unit plus F48 replays cover both loopback addresses

obligations.title: Authorization consumes a canonical IPv4/IPv6 peer identity
obligations.evidence: ipv4_mapped_to_v4 is the verified conversion consumed by access::canonical_ip; the accept boundary and RemoteIP path canonicalize before request context construction, and ip_in_net, Require local, logs, cache and CGI identities use the canonical peer; unit plus dual-stack F49 replays cover mapped deny, allow and local cases

obligations.title: Access-file walk covers every applicable ancestor
obligations.evidence: access_walk_dir_admit states that each ancestor participates when its effective AllowOverride policy permits a layer; collect_layers/apply_req_deferred walk filesystem ancestors without a DocumentRoot or alias-root lower bound, and access_file_layer_read no longer contains an under_root conjunct; unit plus F50 replays cover DocumentRoot parent Basic auth/deny, directory index, CGI, cache lookup and alias-target parents; lexical and canonical AllowOverride identities are conjoined so an explicit None on either path denies the canonical access file (F60-D)

obligations.title: Mapping root comes from URL-selected alias
obligations.evidence: alias_mapping_root_admit states that a root inferred from alias-target containment is never admitted; map_path returns the URL-selected root and dispatch, cache, rewrite reauthorization and --explain pass it to the access walk for RewriteBase/URL-base derivation only; unit plus F51 replays cover overlapping prefix/regex Alias, ScriptAlias and both alias orders

obligations.title: DirectoryIndex cache key and policy bind the selected target
obligations.evidence: cache_directory_index_bind_admit requires an index-selected directory cache entry to bind both key and policy to the index; cache_ignore_query_admit forbids merging dynamic index/script representations across queries; request_scope resolves DirectoryIndex, re-evaluates the index scope and binds the opened index target before lookup/store; unit plus F52 replays cover cross-query CGI indexes and live <Files> denies for directory and direct index URLs

obligations.title: Canonical REQUEST_URI for expressions, rewrites and environment rules
obligations.evidence: request_uri_identity_admit requires REQUEST_URI to be bound to the dispatcher's canonical URL path, query-free and never the raw request-line target. RequestPlan supplies that target to dispatch, cache and --explain; expr::Context::new, Scope::request_env, access::check, rewrite::Context::for_plan and CGI build_env consume the canonical URL path. Require expr/<If>, SetEnvIf Request_URI, RewriteCond and substitution expansion no longer read req.target or append the query string. Unit plus F57 raw-socket replays cover query suffixes, percent-encoded names, dot segments, allow-list and deny-list shapes

obligations.title: One immutable request plan for dispatch, cache, rewrite and explain
obligations.evidence: RequestPlan is built once per request or rewrite round from CanonicalTarget and map_path, collects the access-file layers once, and exposes canonical URL path, mapping root, relative/fs paths, script-alias state and layers. Raw request input enters through WireUrlPath, policy/resource APIs require private-inner DecodedUrlPath, and internally selected directory children enter through the validated single-component FilesystemName type. dispatch_inner_request passes the same plan to cache lookup/store and dispatch; cache no longer re-decodes raw_path or rebuilds mapping; rewrite::Context::for_plan consumes plan identity; --explain prints the plan's canonical path, mapping, layer directories, URL mounts and subjects. Explicit-target plans walk the supplied fs_path itself (never root.join(file_name)), inherit AllowOverride policy from the lexically mapped directory when the root is a symlink, always consume a nonempty layer set, and fail closed when a layer does not belong to the target (explicit_target_layer_admit and target_layer_consume_admit, I60). text_identity_admit rejects non-UTF-8 root, relative and resolved filesystem identities before layer collection, and config/access/MIME parsers reject invalid UTF-8 bytes. Integration coverage exercises cache hits, rewrite rounds, CGI PATH_INFO, DirectoryIndex, explain and the F59 symlinked-root regressions; the universal refinement theorem remains open; pass-10 I61 conjoins the URL-mapped and canonical/rewrite target scopes instead of replacing the lexical scope

obligations.title: Resolved-target scope is a meet with the URL-mapped scope
obligations.evidence: options_conjoin computes the bitwise meet of URL and canonical target Options; handler_conjoin_admit permits an extension only when both identities resolve to the same handler, and conjoined_handlers projects disagreement to RemoveHandler; override_categories_conjoin plus OverridePolicy::conjoined_with make an explicit AllowOverride None on either path identity deny the canonical access file. Scope::restrict_with is consumed by symlink target binding, DirectorySlash/PATH_INFO/FastCGI target reauthorization, rewrite filesystem targets and cache script/index/canonical targets (F60/I61). Content and tagged environment policy are retained from both identities with the URL identity applied last; remove/unset entries from either survive. The Options and AllowOverride-category meets share bits_meet with no-broadening and algebraic lemmas. Unit, htaccess policy, two symlink Apache differentials and F60 end-to-end cases cover handlers, content, environment, -Indexes and AllowOverride denial; SetHandler force conjoins through set_handler_conjoin_admit.

obligations.title: One verified percent-encoding loop for every escape site
obligations.evidence: percent_encode refines to percent_encode_from with out@ equality, a 3x length bound, identity on unmasked input (percent_encode_from_identity) and no-raw-masked-byte output (no_masked_raw/percent_encode_no_masked_raw, given an alphabet-safe mask). Rewrite backreference [B]/[BNE]/[BCTLS]/[BNP] escaping, redirect-Location escaping (which now also escapes non-ASCII bytes instead of emitting Latin-1 mojibake) and the int:escape map all consume the one verified loop; the per-site masks remain runtime data outside Verus and int:unescape remains unverified

obligations.title: Component-aware containment composes across path identities
obligations.evidence: path_under_base_reflexive and path_under_base_transitive mechanize composition of the verified component-aware containment kernel: every base contains itself, and target-under-mid plus mid-under-base implies target-under-base for the lexical byte domain. expr file-test confinement consumes path_under_base. Protected filesystem sinks resolve with mandatory openat2/descriptor binding and FastCGI plus access-file parsing validate descriptor snapshots; configuration testing and startup fail closed when the syscall, required resolution flags, or readable /proc/self/fd descriptor links are unavailable, with no canonicalize/open or lexical-path fallback. SymLinksIfOwnerMatch uses a bounded descriptor-relative walk: every directory and symlink inode is pinned, link bytes are read from the O_PATH descriptor, relative targets remain beneath the root, and the ownership decision is made against the descriptor-resolved target returned to dispatch. Parser-to-path construction remains a refinement boundary. The endpoint-keyed HttpdRsFastCGIStablePath projection is required by default, denies unregistered backends, checks Unix socket owner/inode stability, rejects POSIX ACLs and checks lexical/canonical component ownership and mode against the configured worker UID; only the explicit UnstableFastCgiPaths capability retains the equivalent read-only-tree proof-debt assumption.

obligations.title: Expression parsing is total: malformed input errors, never panics
obligations.evidence: Partial. Parser::regex() bounds-checks that a delimiter exists and rejects a non-ASCII delimiter before advancing Parser::pos, closing P24-A's mid-code-point panic while matching Apache's fail-closed result. Regex and quoted-string accumulators preserve and revalidate UTF-8 bytes instead of producing mojibake. The recursive-descent parser has a MAX_EXPR_DEPTH 64 budget for primary/unary frames; overflow returns Err. Unit tests cover the end-of-operator shape, éé/€€ for =~ and !~, the exact P24 fuzzer artifact, Unicode preservation and depth exhaustion; the live P24 access-file/main-config battery requires clean errors with the process alive, and rewrite_expr retains the crash as a corpus seed with 16,384 smoke executions. A parser-wide mechanized totality refinement remains open.

obligations.title: Rewrite flags and rounds select one target: [PT] maps URLs, overrides are not sticky, dead flags warn
obligations.evidence: RewriteProgramState and rewrite_program_step are the single executable control machine consumed by rewrite::process. rewrite_program_step_spec is the independent mathematical reference transition, and the executable step is proved exactly equal to it for every event. A matched-rule transition itself selects forbidden/gone/no-substitution/expansion precedence; expansion moves to an Expanding phase carrying sealed proxy, redirect, query and round-control flags, and an Expanded observation is rejected in every other phase. Regex/condition results, expanded target classification and filesystem observations enter as explicit observations; the machine owns the rule index, failed-chain resume, query action, bounded [N] restart count, [S]/[L]/[END] precedence, final-pass bit and the unique internal/proxy/redirect/forbidden/gone/restart-limit action. rewrite_program_state_inv proves every successful transition keeps the index and restart count bounded with pending controls only in Expanding, nonactive states are absorbing, and completed restarts cannot exceed the configured limit. The transition composes the previously verified rewrite_chain_resume, rewrite_query_action, rewrite_sink and rewrite_advance kernels, while rewrite_expand_token remains the shared expansion alphabet. Runtime tests cover chain jumps, forbidden precedence, phase-invalid events, sealed expansion flags, restart exhaustion, query action, terminal precedence and stopped/failed absorption. Regex matching, expansion bytes and filesystem facts remain external observations, not competing control-flow implementations.

obligations.title: Signless Options words reset the set like Apache
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H3. Both parsers (config.rs main-config Options arm and htaccess.rs apply_options) now collect recognized signless words into a reset mask and apply push_set(Options::empty()) followed by the mask and the compiled FollowSymLinks default BEFORE the per-word loop, so `Options Indexes` resets the inheritance set exactly as the Apache oracle does: inherited ExecCGI is dropped and the compiled default bits return. Differential coverage agrees on both engines (htaccess-options-absolute-resets-inherited, htaccess-options-none-removes-indexes in tests/config_semantics.py); +/- sign and per-word semantics are unchanged. The runtime options_apply transition now has proofs that Set replaces the parent, Add preserves every existing bit while adding the mask, and Remove cannot grant bits and clears the requested mask.

obligations.title: RewriteMap sources are validated and bounded at load time
obligations.evidence: txt/rnd map loads fail closed when missing, unreadable, invalid UTF-8 or larger than MAX_REWRITEMAP; int maps reject unknown functions. prg helpers resolve against ServerRoot, must be executable regular files no larger than 64 MiB, and are copied from one descriptor snapshot into a sealed memfd. A configuration generation loaded while privileged additionally requires the canonical helper and its parent tree to be root-controlled; root-owned compatibility spellings such as /bin -> /usr/bin remain supported, and the canonical source enters the administrative-input manifest. Each lookup reopens the configured spelling only to verify the original dev/inode/version, then executes the immutable descriptor with a process-group deadline and 8 KiB output cap. Rename replacement, same-inode mutation, service-owned privileged helpers, non-file/oversized helpers, sealing and shebang execution are regression-tested; descriptor_snapshot_admit is the executable identity/version gate.

obligations.title: [CO=...] cookie fields parse under a strict grammar
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H5. build_cookie validates the RFC 6265 grammar before emitting: the cookie name must be an RFC 6265 token, value/Domain/Path must be field-octets (ASCII graphic plus space; ';', ',', '"' and DEL/controls rejected), SameSite only accepts lax|strict|none (case-insensitive) and secure/httponly only their true|1|secure|httponly tokens, so a backref containing ':' or ';' can no longer shift fields or inject attributes and fails closed with Err. The old tolerant '0'/'false' flag spellings were removed and the matching suite expectation was updated to the strict spelling; the compiled flag-file conformance case [CO=TEST:VAL:localhost:3600:/:secure:httponly:none] still conforms. Unit tests: cookie_escape_and_effect_helpers in rewrite.rs.

obligations.title: Raw query bytes reach authorization without lossy conflation
obligations.evidence: ResourceKey.cache_query is Option<Vec<u8>> so raw query strings keep byte identity in cache keys. %{QUERY_STRING} expression evaluation and the rewrite variable fail closed when text is required. At byte-string protocol boundaries, HTTP/WebSocket proxy request lines and CGI QUERY_STRING now preserve every raw query byte instead of using lossy UTF-8; integration/unit tests cover 0xff queries and obs-text headers. The deliberate fail-closed expression/rewrite divergence from Apache remains flagged for review.

obligations.title: .htaccess <IfFile> tests the operator-supplied path
obligations.evidence: Implemented; agent handoff item H7. The .htaccess <IfFile> arm tests exactly one operator-supplied path and the sealed access-program compiler rejects missing or extra operands instead of discarding trailing words. Local Apache 2.4.69 accepts an extra word, so this is tracked as deliberate hardening rather than parity. Apache resolves .htaccess <IfFile> relative paths against ServerRoot while httpd-rs confines .htaccess file probes to relative DocumentRoot paths (F45/I42, CVE-2026-24072/44119); absolute-path .htaccess <IfFile> stays FALSE (a deliberate fail-closed divergence under the user-approved parity waiver).

obligations.title: Every mode rejects silently dropped directives
obligations.evidence: Implemented and strengthened beyond H8. Recognized malformed payloads, known-but-unimplemented directives, and unknown directives are ConfigError values in normal and strict modes. Typed arity/value/context checks cover main config and .htaccess; failonstatus lists cannot be shortened; malformed SSL protocol/passphrase/cache compatibility values and unsupported Header/CustomLog conditions, module LogLevel, cipher policy, compression tuning, rewrite flags, scoped-to-global mutations, vhost balancers, and ignored section children are rejected. This includes Apache 2.4.69's accepted but unsupported <Files> child inside request-time <If>, which ordinary direct requests do not evaluate and whose grant would otherwise broaden httpd-rs access relative to Apache. tests/config_validity.py MALFORMED_CASES requires Apache and both httpd-rs modes to reject shared malformed rows; HARDENED_CASES requires both httpd-rs modes to reject ambiguous legacy forms that Apache accepts. Unit coverage is malformed_directives_fail_in_every_mode plus the exhaustive access/main disposition matrices.

obligations.title: Rewrite rules cannot launder URL policy into an executable target
obligations.evidence: rewrite_scope_retained_admit states that a changed rewrite retains the original URL policy and evaluates the rewritten target; the dispatcher conjoins the original URL's Options/AllowOverride/header policy with the final/rewrite-target scope via restrict_policy_with, while the same-URL target bind performs the full Options+handler meet. RequestPolicyState composes that obligation across URL and filesystem rewrite loops: request_policy_retarget_clears_stale_admission proves both retarget events clear original/target authorization, cache classification and sink admission, while request_policy_retargeted_sink_requires_original_authorization proves a retargeted complete trace cannot omit the original grant. Internal URL/file rewrites, terminal proxy/redirect original gates and cache targets use the shared runtime gate; F60 rewrite-laundering and F23/F53/F58 rewrite regressions exercise the shape. The regex/substitution interpreter remains outside Verus; its security consequence is expressed by the verified state-machine, scope-conjunction and filesystem-containment kernels

obligations.title: Per-directory rewrite URL base, filesystem subject and plan identity
obligations.evidence: request_plan::layer_url_mount is the single URL-mount derivation for access files and main-config <Directory> rewrites; request_plan::layer_subject is the single filesystem-relative RewriteRule subject derivation used by rewrite::subject_for. Every parsed access-file rule carries its layer directory, and htaccess_rewrite_subject_admit requires a derivable subject or fails closed instead of silently skipping a layer. RequestPlan now carries the canonical target, mapping root, relative path, filesystem target and collected access layers for dispatch, cache, rewrite contexts and --explain (I59). Unit plus F53/F58 replays cover prefix Alias, AliasMatch, ScriptAlias, nested .htaccess, explicit RewriteBase, document-root/ancestor layers above the mapping root, and [F]/[G]/[E]/[R] effects

obligations.title: Every non-default handler is dynamic for cache-query isolation
obligations.evidence: cache_dynamic_handler_admit states that a dynamic handler requires a cache bypass; request_scope classifies the effective handler after DirectoryIndex resolution, covering SetHandler proxy:fcgi (direct and index), cgi-script, server-status and future non-default handlers in addition to ProxyPass routes. Unit plus F54 fastcgi-mock replays cover direct and index queries

obligations.title: Cache key material is injective over raw bytes
obligations.evidence: cache_key_hex is refined to cache_key_hex_spec and proved length-preserving and injective (cache_key_hex_spec_injective, hex_byte_spec_injective); base_key hex-encodes server root, host, path, raw query and resolved target bytes, non-UTF-8 URL paths bypass the shared cache, invalid index names are rejected, and invalidation uses the same encoding. Unit plus F55 raw-socket replays cover invalid query bytes versus empty and replacement-byte queries

obligations.title: Local ErrorDocument subrequests are excluded from the original URL cache
obligations.evidence: cache_local_error_document_admit excludes a missing target that can select a local ErrorDocument from lookup/store and refuses to store any response produced by an ErrorDocument internal subrequest (response-provenance marker); existing targets retain normal cache behavior. Unit plus F56 fastcgi-mock replays cover query-dependent local error documents without regressing the Apache cache conformance cases

obligations.title: Only bodyless credential-free GETs with safe response shape enter the cache
obligations.evidence: cache_lookup_request_admit and cache_store_request_admit mechanize bodyless, unframed and credential-free request gates; Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie cannot enter the shared cache, and request no-store independently forbids storage. cache_store_status_admit, cache_store_control_admit, cache_store_shape_admit and cache_store_ttl_admit cover cacheable statuses, response Cache-Control overrides, Set-Cookie/Vary:*/size and positive freshness. cache_remaining_freshness proves origin Age/apparent age cannot increase the freshness lifetime and returns zero once consumed; explicit lifetimes are never raised by CacheMinExpire. cache_ttl_clamp returns zero for reversed CacheMinExpire/CacheMaxExpire instead of panicking on heuristic freshness. Unit matrix plus conformance cache cases exercise each branch

obligations.title: Location shell-glob compiles at parse time (F61)
obligations.evidence: compile_location_pattern builds MatchKind::LocationGlob/LocationMatch/Location at load time; an unhandleable pattern (a bare `~` with no expression, a malformed regex, or a shell pattern above 8190 bytes) is a configuration error and the section is skipped, never an inert literal string. The runtime uses stack-safe bottom-up DP with path_mode=true; exhaustive small-input tests compare it with fnmatch_match/fnmatch_spec, while fnmatch_path_mode_slash_bounded plus fnmatch_class_end_bounds prove the semantic oracle is component-bounded and anchored. fnmatch_location_glob_oracle pins the 2.4.69 probe verdicts. location_wildcard_compiled_admit is debug-asserted at the parse site. A full Verus refinement proof from the iterative DP to fnmatch_spec remains open; F61-A/A2/B/C Python replays cover directive forms and both match-phase placements.

obligations.title: fnmatch class negation honors both markers (F62/F62b)
obligations.evidence: the verified fnmatch specification treats `[^a]` and `[!a]` identically (fnmatch_class_negated, fnmatch_class_body); P27 exhaustive refinement exposed and fixed an older class-body bug that scanned past the closing bracket. fnmatch_class_negation_oracle pins the Apache verdicts for member/non-member basenames in Files globs, Locations and Directory wildcards. The single runtime matcher used by glob_match, Files slots and Location slots is iterative and exhaustively compared with fnmatch_match on small patterns; the old regex translation is gone. Files-class Python replays and the unit matrix cover negated members, escapes, `?` cardinality and basename containment.

obligations.title: expr variables known-set and fail-closed fs vars (F63/F63b)
obligations.evidence: expr_var_known is the single source of truth shared by expr::var evaluation and the load-time validate_vars walker (Expr::Var nodes plus %{...} inside Str with transform-arg recursion). REQUEST_FILENAME/SCRIPT_FILENAME are known only when the context binds fs_path (with_fs_path), so an unbound reference evaluates to Err (fail closed) instead of an empty string; expr_fs_var_bound_admit guards the bound case. Wired at <If>/<ElseIf>, Require expr (unsupported -> fail closed) and RewriteCond expr, in both per-server and per-dir layers. Python replays cover the guard fail-closed and the bound-value forms; the F63b load-time refusal is a config_validity divergence.

obligations.title: SetHandler is a separate precedence field (F64/F64b)
obligations.evidence: SetHandler is parsed into MappingPolicy.set_handler instead of the ordered extension table, so directive order and inheritance cannot reorder it. effective_handler consults the force first (None unforces to the ext table). restrict_with conjoins URL/target forces through set_handler_conjoin_admit with set_handler_conjoin_preserves_force proving a surviving force always comes from one side, and set_handler_precedence_admit is debug-asserted in is_cgi so a force always binds and the ext table can neither remove it nor add execution past it (the attacker .htaccess AddHandler upload chain is dead). [H=...] rewrites write the same field. Python replays cover both directive orders, .htaccess over a SetHandler'ed directory, and the [H] override.

obligations.title: CGI execution needs handler or ScriptAlias plus grant (F65)
obligations.evidence: is_cgi reduces to a single verified kernel call cgi_exec_admit(handler_bound, handler_is_cgi, script_alias, exec_allowed) with cgi_exec_requires_cgi_handler proving no execution without a cgi-script handler bound or a ScriptAlias mapping, and cgi_exec_requires_exec_allowed proving no execution without the Options ExecCGI grant or the alias. A SetHandler default-handler force suppresses a ScriptAlias script; SetHandler None unforces to the ext table. The kernel unit matrix and the F65 replay (source served for a ScriptAlias script under default-handler) pin the behavior.

obligations.title: handler classification uses the lexical basename (F69)
obligations.evidence: the direct dispatch and CGI PATH_INFO split bind classification to the lexical request-mapped basename; FastCGI receives that bound name instead of re-deriving it from SCRIPT_FILENAME. Resolved-target evaluation builds canonical authorization and lexical handler scopes from one immutable RequestPlan/access-layer set, then copies only handlers/set_handler from the lexical Files evaluation. handler_identity_lexical_admit guards classification and handler_scope_lexical_admit proves that a differing resolved target cannot contribute a canonical-only Files/FilesMatch force. Canonical Files authorization remains active. F69 plus five P13 replays cover direct AddHandler, PATH_INFO, FastCGI SetHandler, Files-scoped SetHandler, canonical access denial and live Location controls.

obligations.title: Default-off compatibility surfaces require a process-global capability
obligations.evidence: capability_admit is the executable kernel shared by request parsing, access-file admission and final generated-content/execution sinks; disabled_capability_rejects_request proves a requested surface cannot pass a disabled gate. Main-config compilation records gated effectful directives and validates the final process-global set independent of declaration order; declarations are rejected in vhosts, runtime conditional scopes and access files. Runtime backstops cover TRACE, absolute-form targets, request trailers, autoindex, CGI, FastCGI, the unsafe FastCGI pathname escape hatch and server-status, while program RewriteMap is main-config-only. MutableAuthFiles independently permits service-maintained password/group databases; without it startup, reload and runtime reads consume the verified immutable-file gate. FastCGI configuration requires an exact stable-path policy or the independent UnstableFastCgiPaths capability, and the final handoff checks that gate again. Audit-loaded configurations are marked non-runnable and refused by dispatch so suppressed reporting diagnostics cannot enable legacy authz or program maps. Unit matrices cover every capability, declaration context/final-state behavior, audit-only loading, final sinks and access-file escalation attempts.

obligations.title: Privilege drop and process-control identity fail closed
obligations.evidence: service_identity_admit is consumed before binding/startup and again by drop_privileges; its proofs reject uid/gid zero and require an already-unprivileged process to match both configured effective IDs. pid_control_admit is consumed after pidfd_open and proves that special/non-positive PIDs, UID changes or any recorded identity mismatch cannot reach pidfd_send_signal. Runtime binds the sidecar to boot ID, process start time and executable device/inode, validates root-owned PID artifacts and refreshes the recorded UID after setresuid. Root-owned administrative-input trust is captured before privilege drop and retained across reload; every discovered include/TLS/types/map/proxy-CA parent is checked against the service uid, including empty optional includes, and privileged RewriteMap programs require a root-controlled canonical source before sealing. Reload rejects changes to startup-only identity, pid, root, backlog and listener fields and prepares logs, TLS/OCSP and background generations before one commit point. configuration_generation_admit proves retired generations reject new work; runtime shares one retirement identity across listener loops for the same Config and linearizes H1/H2 admission under a read gate against commit's write gate. It retires only after candidate preparation, closes H1 keep-alive and WebSockets, sends H2 GOAWAY while draining admitted streams, and namespaces access-file IR plus proxy health/failure state until the last old Config drops. A pre-thread root TLS broker accepts only numeric IDs from an exact startup allowlist, closes inherited descriptors and standard streams, disables dumps/new privileges, installs tight rlimits plus a seccomp read-only syscall profile, enforces root-owned stable bounded reads and exits with its parent. Root-capable lifecycle tests cover same-path rotation and mutable replacement rejection; reload integration covers rejected-candidate continuity and successful old-connection retirement. Kernel pidfd/procfs identity semantics, daemon fork orchestration and filesystem ownership enforcement remain outside Verus and are covered by lifecycle/integration tests.

obligations.title: Dynamic backend endpoints remain bound to one configuration identity
obligations.evidence: backend_resolution_binding_admit requires a validated resolver result to belong to the consuming immutable generation, backend_connected_endpoint_admit requires the kernel peer to equal the selected bound endpoint, and fastcgi_peer_identity_admit rejects a Unix listener outside the configured worker/endpoint-owner or uid-0 trust set. Runtime stores the first bounded DNS answer in an Arc-owned per-Config registry shared by proxy, WebSocket, health, TCP FastCGI and OCSP paths; concurrent first answers converge on one map entry, the map has no in-generation expiry, reload creates a distinct registry, and structural Arc lifetime prevents retirement cleanup from racing an in-flight background insertion. Linux strict Unix FastCGI additionally consumes SO_PEERCRED independently of before/after socket pathname metadata. Unit tests cover rebinding, generation separation, structural cleanup, invalid resolver ports, endpoint mismatch and peer uid mismatch; complete workspace tests cover every integrated consumer.
